title: Standard10-preserving 64-hand contextual residual MGDA smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A learned state-by-public-context residual can exploit the admitted 64-hand opponent signal while preserving Standard10: across two seeds, MGDA retains positive worst-group geometry on at least 75% of updates, active-context source agreement remains at least 95% overall/90% every street-seat partition, zero context is exactly base, and the median correct-context policy delta is nonnegative and exceeds the same learned policy under mismatched context.
material_change: Add a 20-feature cross-hand context encoder interacting multiplicatively with native-v6 state features and a hard architectural zero-context identity gate. For each of twelve training opponent-seat groups and two seeds, collect 64 Standard10 warmup hands plus 128 contextual learning hands, train 32 broad MGDA steps, then compare frozen base/correct-context/mismatched-context arms on common decks across all six training and three SHA-disjoint holdout policies.
baseline: Regularized context classification passed at 64 hands (91.67% untouched accuracy, 75% minimum-class, 65.11% normalized unseen-policy entropy), but no learned poker policy has yet consumed that context. Prior context-free broad MGDA preserved Standard10 but had weak/noisy holdout improvement.
notes: This is a small mechanism smoke, not a verdict on asymptotic learning. Failure of implementation/preservation/context-use gates rejects the mechanism; noisy early reward without a mechanistic failure is undertraining evidence and will be judged using cross-seed and correct-vs-mismatched alignment.
Both seeds completed exact independent hand streams and nonempty optimizer states. All MGDA worst-group alignments were positive and zero-context remained exactly Standard10.

Correct-context and cyclically mismatched-context greedy rewards were exactly identical in every evaluated hand for both seeds. This is a concrete inactive-conditioning mechanism result at the current 32-step/128-learning-hands-per-group dose, not an asymptotic rejection based on the negative absolute reward of a small run.

result.summary: Two contextual residual seeds completed 4,608 environment training hands and 9,216 three-arm evaluation hands. Geometry and preservation were sound (99.80% active-context Standard10 agreement), but correct versus mismatched context produced exactly 0 bb/100 in both seeds; base deltas were +0.217 and -2.648 bb/100.
result.conclusion: The architecture trains stably and preserves the external Standard10 prior, yet the current dose does not produce context-dependent greedy behavior. The reward evidence therefore does not justify geometric scaling until a frozen logit-level audit determines whether context signal exists below the argmax boundary or is being ignored by learned weights.
result.next_step: Run a zero-new-hand frozen sensitivity audit over balanced states and all saved 64-hand contexts, measuring logit variance, pairwise context action disagreement, margin crossing distance, and seed consistency before choosing dose or architecture changes.
